summary: Taylor County tower with 1949 Butler Herald notes on foundations, contract and an HQ building; no source found for completion, staffing, fate or the site today.

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts Beulah page files the tower under Taylor County
Quoted Butler Herald material is the source for the 1949 items
September 1949 report: lookout tower to be built near Rupert
evidence.quote: lookout tower to be built near Rupert

evidence.supports: The September report is dated September 22, 1949
Concrete being poured for the tower foundations
evidence.quote: Concrete is being poured this week for the foundations to the lookout tower

evidence.supports: The Melton Vault Co. submitted the lowest bid and won the contract
evidence.quote: The Melton Vault Co., who sent in the lowest bid, was awarded the contract.

evidence.supports: Plan to build the towers in-house to save money
evidence.quote: We are going to build the towers ourselves and thus save a good deal of money

evidence.supports: The December report is dated December 22, 1949
December 1949 report: the one-room building is finished and serves as office and headquarters for the Taylor County Forest Protection Unit
evidence.quote: We have just finished constructing a small one-room building which will serve as office and headquarters for the Taylor County Forest Protection Unit.

evidence.supports: One-room headquarters for the Taylor County Forest Protection Unit, on an acre donated for the lookout tower
evidence.quote: This building is located on the acre of land donated by Mr. W. A. Payne for the lookout tower.
The materials used in constructing the building were given by local citizens interested in the fire protection program.

evidence.supports: Several firms named among the donors of materials
evidence.quote: The materials, including lumber, roofing, windows, and concrete blocks, were donated by Messrs. Frank Gray, L.L. Minor Lumber Co., Reid Lumber Co., Hayward Brothers and Melton Vault Co.

evidence.supports: Hope for one tower in operation by the first of the year; the report does not name which tower
evidence.quote: We hope to have one tower in operation by the first of the year.

evidence.supports: tnlandforms list: Beulah Lookout Tower in Taylor County, elevation 653

events.note: Concrete foundations being poured for a lookout tower to be built near Rupert, and The Melton Vault Co. awarded the contract (Butler Herald report of September 22, 1949, as quoted on the Forest Lookouts page).
One-room headquarters for the Taylor County Forest Protection Unit finished on an acre donated for the lookout tower (Butler Herald report of December 22, 1949).

sources.title: Beulah - Forest Lookouts (quoting the Butler Herald, 1949)

notes_for_editor: The 1949 material is quoted secondhand from the Butler Herald on a lookout-history site; the newspaper itself was not reached. The 1949 items never name Beulah, so the link between the Beulah page, the 'near Rupert' tower and the tnlandforms Beulah Lookout Tower rests on the page's Taylor County heading and is unverified. Two WebSearch passes (Taylor County tower, Rupert 1949) found nothing further; a Rupert location fact was not fetched and is not in the story. Suggest the Butler Herald archive, the Georgia Forestry Commission history staff, or the Taylor County historical society for completion and later history.
